lines.source: Hypothetical planning scenario, not measured robot performance.
lines.text: The AI finds a plan. The moment has already passed. In a moving machine, a good answer can arrive too late.

lines.source: lab-deadline-model.js: synthetic periodic jobs, deadline one period after release.
lines.text: In this experiment, the controller must act on every beat. It cannot pause the world while a model thinks.

lines.source: Chosen latency pattern, not a claim that every inference system lacks a timing bound.
lines.text: The model answers quickly, until one request takes longer. A fast average tells us little about that missed moment.

lines.source: Synthetic blocking baseline: unfinished work queues later controller jobs.
lines.text: Put that request in the controller's path. The controller waits, then the work behind it waits too. One delay becomes a queue.

lines.source: Synthetic async design: fixed controller and admission costs, bounded handoff and isolated worker assumed.
lines.text: Give the model a different role. It proposes; the controller decides when to use a proposal. Inference no longer blocks this loop.

lines.source: Observation age and context validity differ from result arrival time.
lines.text: But the clock is only half the story. A plan can arrive now and still describe a state that has already changed.

lines.source: lab-deadline-model.js checks observation timestamp and context version. Baseline safety is not simulated.
lines.text: Stamp the observation, not just the arrival. Check its age and context before use. Otherwise, use the baseline controller.

lines.source: Architecture proposal: timing and freshness do not prove action safety; no plant is simulated.
lines.text: That is permission to be considered, not proof the action is safe. Action limits and the baseline need their own evidence.

lines.source: Injected shared stalls in lab-deadline-model.js. Asynchrony alone proves neither isolation nor a worst-case timing bound.
lines.text: Now let both share a constrained resource. The deadline breaks again. Asynchrony removes a dependency; resource isolation and worst-case analysis remain separate jobs.

lines.source: Dr. Ozgur Ural's open architecture experiment. Timing is simulated; task success and proposal usefulness are not measured.
lines.text: This is my architecture experiment, not a robot benchmark. Ask two questions: did the controller act on time, and was the AI proposal still useful?
